Attic floor insulation should be installed last. While highly effective, it must follow air and duct sealing to avoid covering up critical areas that require sealing and to ensure ducts running through the attic are properly sealed and insulated beforehand. Therefore, we assume that upgrades will be implemented in the following sequence: Advanced air sealing is applied first to applicable dwelling units, with the goal of achieving 5 ACH50.While some regions require tighter envelopes for new construction, 5 ACH50 reflects the average infiltration rate achieved in empirical studies across representative climate zones and ensures that selected homes do not already comply with 2024 IECC requirements (Phoung, Lou, & White, 2025a). After air sealing, HVAC ducts in applicable homes are sealed and insulated to achieve the following: • A maximum of 5% duct air leakage to the outside • Duct insulation level of R-8. Attic floor insulation is the upgraded in applicable dwelling units to the following levels: • R-49 in climate zone 1 • R-60 in climate zones 2 through 8. More details about the modeling assumptions for these three measures can be found in the accompanying documentation (Phoung, Lou, & White, 2025a) (Phoung, Lou, & White, 2025b) (Lou & Liu, 2025). 3 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 2 Applicability Advanced air sealing upgrades are applied to dwelling units with infiltration rates greater than or equal to 6 ACH50. Attic floor insulation upgrades are applied only to dwelling units with unfinished attics (vented and unvented attic types in ResStock). Specifically, upgrades are triggered when attic floor insulation is below the following levels: less than R-49 in climate zone 1 and less than R-60 in climate zones 2 through 8. Duct sealing applies to dwelling units with duct leakage to the outside greater than 6% or duct insulation rated below R-6. Dwelling units with 0% leakage to the outside and uninsulated ducts are not applicable, as these configurations typically indicate that the ducts are located entirely within conditioned spaces. Further details on the applicability criteria and stock saturation for each of these three measures can be found in the accompanying documentation (Phoung, Lou, & White, 2025a) (Phoung, Lou, & White, 2025b) (Lou & Liu, 2025). Table 1 summarizes the stock saturation for the upgrade package that includes all three measures. This comprehensive package is applicable to approximately 97.9% of the U.S. housing stock. However, most homes receive only one or some of these upgrades. Only 27.8% of homes receive all three upgrades. Table 1.
